**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/04/22 (Sat) 11:59
- [USER] User asked for an explanation of the difference between MIDI and MP3 files.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] MIDI (Musical Instrument Digital Interface) is a file format that represents music in a digital form.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] MIDI is not an audio file format like MP3, but rather a way to represent musical information such as notes, pitches, and timing.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] MIDI files do not contain any actual audio data, but rather a series of instructions for how to generate music.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] MP3 is an audio file format that stores actual audio data as a series of digital audio samples.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] MP3 files are compressed versions of audio files that can be played on a wide range of devices, including computers, phones, and portable music players.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] One key difference between MIDI and MP3 files is that MIDI files are much smaller in size since they do not contain any actual audio data.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] MIDI files are easy to transmit and store, but they require a device that can interpret the MIDI data and generate sound from it.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] MP3 files contain audio data and can be played directly on most devices without the need for any additional software.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Another difference between MIDI and MP3 files is the level of detail and complexity that they can represent.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] MIDI files can represent a wide range of musical information, including specific notes, pitches, and timing, as well as more complex details such as expression and articulation.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] MP3 files are limited to representing audio data and do not have the same level of detail or flexibility as MIDI files.
